chunks: And by this same chain, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a group of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, who relates it marfūʿ from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (peace be upon him):

He said: 'When a man dies on a ship and it is not possible to [reach] the shore, he said: he is to be shrouded and embalmed with ḥanūṭ in a garment, the funeral prayer is to be performed over him, and he is to be cast into the water.'

key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: he raises it (marfūʿ — the narrator attributes it directly to the Imam, omitting any intermediate link)
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: he is embalmed with ḥanūṭ (camphor-based funerary preparation applied to joints and points of prostration)
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is shrouded (wrapped in the burial cloth, kafan)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Imam al-Ṣādiq (AS) for a person who dies on a ship and cannot be brought to shore for burial?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq (AS), transmitted via a marfūʿ chain through Sahl ibn Ziyād, establishes the jurisprudential ruling for a Muslim who dies aboard a ship when it is impossible to bring the body ashore. The Imam rules that the deceased is to be shrouded in the kafan, embalmed with ḥanūṭ (a camphor-based funerary preparation) inside a garment, have the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah) performed over him, and then be cast into the water.
